conventions.convention: Hilbert inner products are linear in the first argument. A normal density state means the bounded trace pairing represented by a positive trace-class operator of trace one on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space; equivalence with other notions of normality is not asserted.

Unbounded observable means and variances are scalar spectral integrals. The mean requires a finite absolute first moment; variance requires a finite second moment. These expressions do not authorize arbitrary products of an unbounded observable with a density.

Support is the orthogonal complement of the kernel. Logarithms are natural, taken on positive supports; zero eigenvalues contribute zero to entropy. Infinite relative entropy is defined only on the stated domains, without assigning a value to infinity minus infinity.
The entropy scale k_B is positive, in J/K; temperature is positive and β=1/(k_B T) has units J⁻¹. Hamiltonians and free energies are in joules, and Gibbs exponents are dimensionless.
Real-time evolution is U(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ), Heisenberg evolution is U(t)* A U(t), and the KMS boundary is at t+iβℏ. Time is in seconds and ℏ is in J s. The KMS assertion is finite-dimensional.

The control Hamiltonian is H(h)=H₀−hB. Static susceptibility uses β times the Kubo–Mori covariance; equality with β times ordinary variance holds exactly when B commutes with the Gibbs density, equivalently with H(h).

The canonical purification uses a supplied ordered basis and its identified reference copy. Its marginal is basis independent, but the purification vector itself is not asserted to be basis independent. Circuit error bounds are conditional on successful output and the certified shift event; trace distance includes the factor one half.

Grand preparation uses specified maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains and a common finite or countable eigenbasis, with nonnegative integer particle counts. Differentiation additionally requires compact-parameter summable joint second-moment envelopes.

load_bearing.statement: Every Hermitian endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension D≥1 has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. Its finite spectral functional calculus and trace are basis independent; the density-weighted form satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz; rank-one densities are exactly the pure and extreme finite densities.

For a trace-class normal density on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, bounded trace pairing is given by its absolutely convergent spectral expansion and is cyclic with bounded operators. A self-adjoint observable gives a scalar spectral probability law; moments require their stated integrability domains. Entropy may be infinite, and countable convex mixtures converge in trace norm.
For trace-class normal densities ρ,σ on a separable complex Hilbert space with supp ρ⊆supp σ, finite C(ρ,σ) implies finite S(ρ) and D(ρ∥σ)=C(ρ,σ)−S(ρ)/k_B≥0, with equality exactly when ρ=σ.

Assuming AC, a densely defined self-adjoint Hamiltonian on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, bounded below and with trace-class Gibbs exponential throughout an open positive-β interval, has finite positive partition function and faithful normal Gibbs density. Every normal density with finite absolute spectral form energy has finite entropy and satisfies E_A(ρ)−TS(ρ)≥F_β, with equality exactly at the Gibbs density; the Gibbs entropy identity also holds.

For nonzero finite-dimensional H, B(H) with its ordinary operator norm is a unital complex C*-algebra. Every positive complex-linear functional is uniquely Tr(ρA) for a positive semidefinite ρ, with functional norm Tr ρ=ω(I); states correspond exactly to density matrices.

For a continuously differentiable finite Hermitian matrix path, the exponential derivative is the Duhamel integral. For affine Hermitian controls, the Hessian of log Tr exp M is the Kubo–Mori covariance, whose diagonal is nonnegative and at most ordinary variance, with equality exactly in the commuting case.
